callouts.p: The mirror lets readers see the change clearly and shows that the same situations offer the same choices: Scrooge simply chooses differently.

head: Stave 1
Stave 5
rows: Grudges Bob a day off; one coal
Raises Bob’s salary; ‘Make up the fires’

bullets: Spatial: Scrooge travels across time and space (his school, Fezziwig’s warehouse, the Cratchits’ home, a lighthouse, a ship, the thieves’ den, the churchyard).
Moral: from sin to repentance to redemption.
Emotional: cold → nostalgic → sympathetic → terrified → joyful.
Time compression: everything in one night.
Stave 1 ends with Scrooge going to bed ‘without undressing’.
Stave 2 ends with him extinguishing the light and falling asleep.
Stave 3 ends with the hooded phantom approaching.
Stave 4 ends with the phantom becoming a bedpost.
Stave 5 ends with ‘God bless Us, Every One!’
core.p: Each stave ends with Scrooge alone in bed or at a moment of change, creating suspense and rhythm.

exam.q: Explain how Dickens uses structure to present Scrooge’s transformation. (20 marks)
exam.tip: Use the comparison table as your plan.

mistakes.r: It is linear in time but cyclical in its mirroring of Stave 1.
mistakes.w: Saying the structure is linear only.

quotes.a: Opening on death sets up the ghost story.
quotes.q: Marley was dead: to begin with.

summary: The five-stave structure takes Scrooge on a cyclical journey from Christmas Eve to Christmas morning, through past, present and future, with Stave 5 deliberately mirroring Stave 1 so the reader can measure his transformation.

terms.d: Exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, resolution.
